the_day: OpenAI completed an $11 billion funding round at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation, Anthropic was reported to be starting its IPO roadshow next week and Claude gained bank-account linking, Google was sued over its school AI, and Meta and xAI were quiet.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly plans to start its IPO roadshow next week
points: Unconfirmed: the Financial Times and The Information report that Anthropic will begin its IPO roadshow next week, despite the tech selloff.
Dealroom, citing the FT, says Anthropic aims to raise $80B to $100B at a valuation of $1.25T to $1.75T.
CNBC reports that some investors call a $1.5 trillion valuation 'a stretch' after the AI stock selloff.

items.headline: Claude can now link bank accounts and analyze transactions
points: Yahoo Finance and 24/7 Wall St. report that Claude can now connect to users' bank accounts and analyze their transactions.
PYMNTS calls the feature Claude Personal Finance and says it launched ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq listing.
Yahoo Finance reports that Claude will not give investment advice.

items.headline: Researchers find Claude Code approval files exposing secrets on GitHub
points: Apirro researchers say files created by Claude Code's 'Yes, and don't ask again' option exposed passwords and API keys in public GitHub repositories.
GBHackers reports 2,539 secrets across 1,994 repositories, and The Hacker News counts 1,122 public copies of the file.
None of the cited items is an Anthropic post.
items.for_you: Developers using Claude Code should check that its approval settings file is not committed to public repositories.

points: PSI announced a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture that it says was produced with help from an Anthropic model.

The claim comes from PSI. None of the cited items is an Anthropic post.

items.headline: OpenAI raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, reports say
points: Bloomberg reports that OpenAI completed an $11 billion portion of its funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation. Reuters reported the same, citing a source.
The American Bazaar says the round fell short of a $30 billion target, and 24/7 Wall St. says OpenAI first sought $1.4 trillion.
The Information reports that OpenAI is expected to brief investors next week.
